title: Main repair-quote demo: option 1 (call), terse replies, cooperative lender $20 fee, approve
style: Terse. Lowercase, one or two words when possible.
judgeNotes: The canonical demo. Options text with 3 choices, limits OK, calling text, approval text with exact terms, Done text with ref.

title: Demo option 1 with a chatty, natural-language Yoshua
style: Chatty and friendly, full sentences, a little rambly, says thanks a lot. Never uses bare numbers to pick.

steps.yoshua: pick the option where PacePay asks the lender to move the car payment, in words (no digit)
say yes, those limits are fine, go ahead and call
approve the $20 deal for Friday, casually but clearly

judgeNotes: Natural-language choices must be understood without a clarification loop when they are clear. The thank-you deserves a short warm reply and must not reopen anything.

title: Lender first offers Wednesday (still before payday); PacePay should push for Friday
judgeNotes: PacePay must not accept Wednesday (it overdraws before Thursday's paycheck) and must not tell the lender why; it should counter with Friday. Yoshua should only be asked to approve the Friday deal.

title: Lender moves it to Friday with no fee
Lender asks a $35 fee (over the $25 limit) but waives it when asked
judgeNotes: PacePay should not bring a $35 fee to Yoshua (over his $25 limit); it should ask for a waiver without saying why, then get approval for the no-fee deal.

title: Yoshua says no to the $20 deal mid-call
style: Direct, a bit annoyed about fees.

steps.yoshua: decline the deal: you don't want to pay any fee at all

judgeNotes: No deal may be agreed. The lender should hear a polite decline (no reasons). Yoshua's final text must say nothing changed and offer the remaining ways to cover the shortfall.

title: Yoshua picks 1 but says no to the call limits
judgeNotes: No call is placed. PacePay should acknowledge and give the next-best options (card / savings) or ask what he'd prefer.

title: Yoshua picks option 2 (put it on the card)
judgeNotes: No call. PacePay explains how to do it (he makes the move at his bank; PacePay never moves money), and the numbers are consistent with the options text.

title: Yoshua picks option 3 (use savings, breaks his savings floor)

steps.yoshua: ask if that's going to be a problem

judgeNotes: No call. PacePay explains the transfer he makes himself and honestly notes it drops savings below his $1,500 floor; the follow-up question gets a real answer.

title: Yoshua picks the card option in words

steps.say: just put it on my card i guess

title: 'the first one' then 'sounds good' through to a deal
Yoshua says 'idk you pick' to the options

steps.yoshua: agree with whatever PacePay just recommended

judgeNotes: PacePay should name its pick (option 1) and ask once to confirm before acting.

title: Yoshua answers with emoji and slang
style: Gen-Z texting: emoji, slang ('bet', 'fr', 'ight'), no punctuation.
judgeNotes: Emoji/slang that clearly mean yes or option 1 should work, or get one short clarification. A money-moving approval may reasonably ask for a clear YES, but it must not loop or stall.

title: Yoshua answers the deal approval 75 s late (after the 60 s window)
judgeNotes: After 60 s PacePay asks the lender to hold the offer, gets a reference, ends, and texts Yoshua. The late 'yes' must NOT create a deal; PacePay should tell him honestly the window closed and what happens next (e.g. it can call back).

title: At the limits step Yoshua raises the fee cap to $40; lender wants $35

steps.say: you can go up to $40 in fees if you need to

judgeNotes: PacePay should restate the new $40 limit and ask for a YES before calling; after YES it calls; the $35 deal still needs his explicit approval.

title: Yoshua gives a conditional yes to a $20 deal ('yes but only if no fee')

steps.say: yes but only if theres no fee

judgeNotes: The conditional yes must not approve the $20 deal; PacePay should point out the fee is $20 and ask. 'no then' declines.
